_notes: 2026-08-28: Two things shipped. (1) Row-level CSV export (61dca03) — /reports is pre-aggregated so every new question meant a new report view; now /api/export/calls.csv (login_required), /api/export/queue-calls.csv (manager_required) and /api/export/data-dictionary.md, with buttons on /reports carrying the selected period. Two files because call_log has NO wait metric — that lives in queued_calls. Scoping was inline in the /reports route; extracted to resolve_visible_emails() in reporting_service.py and shared, and an empty team list now matches NOTHING rather than falling through to no filter (same class of mistake as the 2026-07-30 caller-ID [0] fallback). Customer PII off by default, admin-only behind ?include_customer=1; every row instead carries customer_ref, a per-tenant salted hash of the caller's LAST 9 DIGITS (first cut hashed all digits and split +61412345678 from 0412345678 into two people — caught in test). queue-calls.csv is manager-only AND deliberately unscoped by agent, because abandoned calls have no answered_by and an agent filter would report a zero abandon rate rather than an honest one. The data dictionary is load-bearing, not decoration: transfer rows inflating call volume (gotcha 29), UTC vs Sydney, null talk_seconds. NEVER RUN AGAINST WATSON'S REAL DATA — no tenant DB locally, verified only against a temp DB with fabricated rows. (2) Deleted the dead Admins card on /admin (ee55785). Rinq had TWO role stores and only one counted: the `permissions` table (tenant DB) was written by the card and read by exactly one line — the one drawing that same card. db.get_permission(email) had zero callers anywhere. tenant_users.role (master DB) is what get_current_user() actually reads. 95698c8 (2026-04-08) added `permissions` as the first local replacement for Watson's Grant service; 4e125e9 (2026-04-16) superseded it with tenant_users.role and /admin/users, but the card was never removed and read as authoritative. Clare sat in it looking like an admin while her real role was 'user', which is why /reports showed her only Carol — her one reports_to reportee. Diagnosed by querying production directly rather than inferring from code; all three tables matched exactly. Card + its two routes deleted (160 lines); the permissions table and LocalPermissionService left as the PermissionService interface impl — DO NOT wire them up.
